properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 7:57PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 757 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
La Joya, or 21 miles north of Socorro, moving north at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Belen, Veguita, Casa Colorada, Jarales, Bernardo, Rio Communities,
Los Trujillos-Gabaldon, La Joya, Los Chaves and Tome.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 60 between Mile Markers 166 and 178. Interstate 25 between
Mile Markers 161 and 198.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Motorists can expect brief but sudden changes in visibility and
ponding of water on roadways as storms move through the area.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 7:54PM MDT until October 24 at 10:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Mineral County and Rio Grande County...

* WHEN...Until 1015 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will continue along and near the Rio Grande this
evening, especially from near Del Norte to below Monte Vista.
Several roads remain closed and housing areas evacuated due to high
water. While many rivers and streams have already crested, flooding
and high flows will continue tonight, especially around Monte
Vista.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 754 PM MDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring.
- Please continue to heed any road closures.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Rio Grande from Del Norte to Monte Vista.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
SVREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southeastern Otero County in south central New Mexico...
Northeastern Hudspeth County in western Texas...

Dell City, moving northeast at 50 mph.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 7:50PM MDT until October 28 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...From this evening to Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 19.5 feet, the water level in the Lower Rio Puerco
will begin to threaten several homes and structures in the village
of San Francisco between Interstate 25 and the Rio Grande. Further
rises in water levels would begin to flood the village of San
Francisco.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 PM MDT Saturday the stage was 6.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...While the timing may change, the river is currently
expected to rise above flood stage early Wednesday afternoon to a
crest of 19.6 feet Wednesday evening. It will then fall below
flood stage early Thursday morning.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Sunday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 7:45PM MDT until October 26 at 11:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Eastern Kane County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the San Juan River is occurring.
Low-water crossings will be inundated with water and may not be
passable. The river is running fast and high. Do not attempt to
cross.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 743 PM MDT, the San Juan River is forecast to continue to rise
and crest near 6 PM Sunday at Bluff above moderate flood stage.
Flooding will continue downstream to the terminus at Lake Powell
through at least late Monday morning.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The San Juan River from downstream of Bluff to the terminus at
Lake Powell.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away. River banks can become unstable and
unsafe.

properties.description:

or 23 miles southwest of Los Alamos, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 24 at 9:42PM EDT until October 25 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 6 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to
two feet of inundation above ground level expected along
shorelines and tidal waterways (7.9 to 8.1 feet Mean Lower Low
Water at Charleston).

* WHERE...Coastal Colleton and Charleston Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Monday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM to 11 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Significant saltwater inundation will render
numerous roads impassable. Properties may also flood.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 7:34 AM Sunday
at Charleston. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

reach of the Rio Ojo Caliente are flooded.  Private roadways within

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 9:21PM AST until October 27 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches along the northwest to northeast coast of
Puerto Rico and Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 24 at 3:10PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
ESFHFO

A significant pattern change is expected Monday night through at
least Thursday as deep tropical moisture is brought north. A
combination of surface lows and troughs will bring exceptionally
moist air over the eastern end of the state beginning Monday night
and extending to all islands Tuesday. Heavy rain and thunderstorms
are possible throughout this period. Models have not converged on
details yet, so exact locations, timing, and rainfall amounts are not
certain. Please be prepared for periods of heavy rain this coming
week.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through the
Internet (weather.gov/hawaii), local media, social media, or NOAA
Weather Radio broadcasts.

An updated outlook will be issued Sunday by 6 AM HST or sooner if
necessary.
